title: Optimize walkthrough: quant profiles INT8/FP8 - quality vs latency - Atlas ML
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Atlas ML through Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), demoed the Console quality-vs-latency dashboard, and discussed benchmark plan. Customer concerned about quality regressions on long-context summarization and latency targets for real-time inference; requested sample benchmarks, quant profile docs, and a 2-week pilot with canary traffic on Dedicated. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Console demo: Optimize dashboard and profiles
action_items: Priya Desai - Share INT8/FP8 quantization profile docs + sample config - due 2026-07-23
Jordan Kim - Send pricing for 2-week Dedicated pilot and expected credits - due 2026-07-22
Ben Carter (Atlas) - Provide 3 representative prompt sets (summaries, extractive QA, chat) - due 2026-07-24
Priya Desai - Run initial perf benchmark on Atlas sample prompts (latency P50/P95 and quality BLEU/ROUGE) - due 2026-07-28
Leila Morales - Confirm internal pilot stakeholders and compliance checklist - due 2026-07-25
next_steps: Priya to upload quant profiles doc to shared drive
Jordan to send pilot pricing and contract template
Atlas to share prompt sets and expected SLOs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we'll do a quick intro, then Priya will walk through quantization profiles and the Optimize console.
[00:07] Leila Morales: hi, thanks. quick note we have Samir and Ben on the line, ben will be the primary for the technical bits.
[00:12] Ben Carter: yep, hi all. our main goal is to drop per-token cost while keeping summarization quality over long docs, and hit a 150ms P50 for short chat hits.
[00:20] Priya Desai: great, that's helpful. so we'll focus on INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, and demo the quality vs latency plots from Optimize so you can see where the knee is.
[00:29] Jing Wei: quick question, are we assuming hosted or Dedicated for the pilot?
[00:32] Jordan Kim: good q; Atlas indicated they'd prefer Dedicated for isolation and predictable latency but open to hosted for quick bench. today we'll show both options and how quant profiles behave.
[00:40] [00:45] Priya Desai: ok slide-ish start, so quantization basically reduces weight precision to lower memory and improve throughput. INT8 is more aggressive and often gives bigger speedups, FP8 sits between FP16 and INT8 in terms of quality drop. key point: profile matters per-op and per-layer.
[00:58] Ben Carter: i've seen INT8 induce some hallucinations on summarization tasks in other runs, is that typical?
[01:03] Priya Desai: yes, on generative summarization you can see small regressions, especially with long context. our Optimize recommends per-model profiles — e.g., hybrid profiles where decoder layers use higher precision while attention heads run INT8. that preserves quality while getting most of the latency gains.
[01:20] Leila Morales: what's the typical latency improvement number we can expect?
[01:24] Priya Desai: depends on hardware; on A100-class GPUs INT8 can be 1.8-2.5x faster per-token vs FP16; FP8 often gives ~1.3-1.8x with much lower quality impact. on newer Ampere/Blackwell variants it improves more. we should run Atlas prompts to quantify.
[01:40] Samir Patel: our SRE cares about tail latency. does quantization increase P95 jitter?
[01:44] Priya Desai: good callout. generally batching and server-side kernel selection are the bigger factors for tail latency. quantization can reduce compute time so tails often shrink, but mixed precision kernels or fallback paths can add variance. we test P50/P95 in the benchmark and report it.
[01:58] [02:05] Jordan Kim: real quick, competitors question — we've seen folks evaluate OpenAI and Anthropic; but they don't give the same model/quant control we do. Redwood lets you pick profiles and run canary rollouts.
[02:15] Ben Carter: right that's attractive. can you show the Console?
[02:19] Priya Desai: yep sharing screen now - sorry transcript may garble some names.
[02:25] [screen share noises]
[02:30] Priya Desai: this is the Optimize dashboard — quality vs latency. on the x axis latency, y axis quality (we use task-specific metrics you provide). each point is a profile: FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8 hybrid, full INT8. you can click a profile to view per-layer heatmaps and recommended rollback policies.
[02:50] Ben Carter: nice, can we set automatic rollback if quality drops by more than 2%?
[02:54] Priya Desai: yes, you can create a policy tied to your eval set. Optimize will monitor and do automated fallback to a safer profile or a higher-precision model.
[03:04] Jing Wei: what's the workflow to try it on our dataset?
[03:07] Priya Desai: upload your prompt set (or point to an S3 bucket), choose the eval metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, embedding-sim threshold, whatever you use), then run a distributed benchmark; results populate here.
[03:16] Ben Carter: how long does the benchmark take for ~5k prompts?
[03:19] Priya Desai: depends on batch sizing and concurrency; usually a few hours on a small Dedicated pool, or 6-8 hours if running lower-cost hosted. we can parallelize.
[03:27] [03:30] Priya Desai: showing a sample run — here's an Atlas-like summarization eval: FP16 baseline ROUGE-L 35.2, FP8 34.8 (-0.4), INT8 hybrid 35.0 (-0.2) and full INT8 33.5 (-1.7). latency: FP16 210ms P50, FP8 150ms, INT8 hybrid 110ms, full INT8 95ms.
[03:52] Leila Morales: okay those numbers are promising; full INT8 drop of 1.7 might be too much but hybrid looks good.
[03:58] Ben Carter: what's the effort to implement hybrid? is it automatic?
[04:01] Priya Desai: Optimize provides recommended hybrid profiles per-model. you can also tune layer masks; SEs can generate a profile using our calibration harness and provide a reproducible quant config. most customers use the recommended profiles and then tweak with a small eval loop.
[04:15] Samir Patel: security question — if we run the pilot on Dedicated, will our data stay in our VPC?
[04:20] Jordan Kim: yes Dedicated deployments can be VPC-isolated; we also support customer-managed KMS for keys and have audit logs. we'll send the security whitepaper.
[04:28] Jing Wei: can you run the pilot with a canary percentage? we want 10% of production traffic routed to Redwood first.
[04:32] Jordan Kim: absolutely; rollout policies support percentage-based canaries and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[04:38] [04:40] Priya Desai: back to profiles — note that prompt engineering also interacts a lot with quantization; sometimes small prompt tweaks reduce sensitivity to lower precision. we recommend freezing the eval prompts and testing prompts with both profiles.
[04:53] Ben Carter: good to know. do you have a recommended threshold for acceptable quality delta?
[04:57] Priya Desai: we usually suggest <0.5% absolute on task metric for high-stakes production (like summarization), but customers set their own SLA. for exploratory workloads 1-2% might be acceptable given 2x latency gains.
[05:08] Leila Morales: pricing — how do we account for Dedicated pilot costs vs hosted?
[05:12] Jordan Kim: we'll send a pilot pricing sheet; Dedicated is committed but we can do short-term trial capacity. Jordan to follow up with numbers (action item).
[05:20] Ben Carter: one more technical — long-context KV cache size and memory pressure with INT8?
[05:24] Priya Desai: quantized weights reduce model memory; KV cache primarily driven by sequence length and token type. INT8 helps a bit but watch GPU memory for long context. Optimize will surface memory vs latency tradeoffs too.
[05:38] [05:45] Jing Wei: any caveats on model types? like decoder-only vs encoder-decoder?
[05:49] Priya Desai: encoder-decoder models can behave differently; quantization can interact with cross-attention layers. our profiling includes model-architecture specific heuristics.
[05:58] Ben Carter: curious — do you support FP8 variants like E4M3 vs E5M2?
[06:03] Priya Desai: we support the common FP8 formats our runtime can run; Optimize labels them and indicates expected numeric range; we can include the specific format in the docs we share.
[06:12] Jordan Kim: ok, let's recenter. agreed actions: Priya will send quant profiles and run an initial perf bench on the prompts Ben shares; Jordan will send pilot pricing and contract; Atlas will share prompts and SLOs.
[06:24] Leila Morales: timeline — we need pilot running by early August ideally.
[06:28] Jordan Kim: sounds feasible; we'll aim to have bench results within a week of receiving prompts.
[06:33] [06:35] Ben Carter: also, for the quality metrics, can you compute both ROUGE and embedding-sim so we can compare extractive vs abstractive quality?
[06:41] Priya Desai: yes we can add both, and show side-by-side plots.
[06:45] Jing Wei: any compliance concerns for EU data? some docs will be EU-resident.
[06:49] Jordan Kim: Redwood supports region pinning and data residency controls; we'll include the compliance brief.
[06:55] [07:00] Priya Desai: brief demo end — open for Qs.
[07:03] Ben Carter: couple tiny transcription errors in the demo but content is clear. overall very helpful.
[07:09] Leila Morales: next steps confirmed. Jordan, Priya thanks.
[07:12] Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and pricing. talk soon.
[07:16] [end of meeting]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and truncation; timestamps are approximations. many customers refer to "Optimize" console internal features — some names may be slightly transcribed (e.g., "hybrid profile" typed as "hybrid profile").
